DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS
FOR WILLOW BEND ESTATES

THIS DECLARATION is made on August 3, 2026 by Willow Bend Development Company LLC, a Texas limited liability company (the "Declarant").

RECITALS

A. The Declarant is the owner of the real property in Collin County, Texas described as Willow Bend Estates, Phase One, according to the plat recorded on June 18, 2026 at Document No. 2026-0084417 in the Official Public Records of Collin County, Texas (the "Property").

B. The Declarant intends to develop the Property as a residential subdivision and to subject it to the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, and liens set forth in this Declaration, all of which run with the land and bind every person acquiring any interest in the Property.

NOW, THEREFORE, the Declarant declares that the Property is held, transferred, sold, conveyed, and occupied subject to the following:

ARTICLE I. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Association" means Willow Bend Estates Homeowners Association, Inc., a Texas nonprofit corporation.

1.2 "Common Area" means all real property owned by the Association for the common use and enjoyment of the Owners, including the entry monuments, private streets, detention pond, and landscape easements shown on the plat.

1.3 "Lot" means any numbered plot of land shown on the recorded plat, other than the Common Area.

1.4 "Owner" means the record owner of the fee simple title to any Lot, excluding a person holding an interest merely as security for the performance of an obligation.

1.5 "Board" means the board of directors of the Association.

ARTICLE II. PROPERTY RIGHTS

2.1 Owners' Easement of Enjoyment. Every Owner has a right and easement of enjoyment in and to the Common Area, which is appurtenant to and passes with title to every Lot, subject to the Association's right to suspend that right for any period during which an assessment remains unpaid for more than thirty (30) days, and for a period not to exceed sixty (60) days for any infraction of the published rules.

2.2 Delegation of Use. An Owner may delegate the right of enjoyment to the members of the Owner's family, tenants, and invitees.

ARTICLE III. MEMBERSHIP AND VOTING

3.1 Membership. Every Owner is a member of the Association. Membership is appurtenant to and may not be separated from ownership of a Lot.

3.2 Voting. Each Lot carries one vote. When more than one person holds an interest in a Lot, the vote for that Lot must be cast as those persons determine among themselves, and in no event may more than one vote be cast for any Lot.

ARTICLE IV. ASSESSMENTS

4.1 Creation of the Lien and Personal Obligation. Each Owner, by accepting a deed to a Lot, covenants to pay the Association: (a) annual assessments and (b) special assessments for capital improvements. Each assessment, together with interest, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees, is a charge on the Lot and a continuing lien on the Lot from the date the assessment becomes due, and is also the personal obligation of the person who was the Owner when the assessment became due.

4.2 Purpose. Assessments shall be used to promote the health, safety, and welfare of the residents and for the improvement and maintenance of the Common Area.

4.3 Annual Assessment. The annual assessment for the calendar year 2027 is $1,150 per Lot, payable in two equal installments due on January 15 and July 15 of each year. The Board may increase the annual assessment by not more than ten percent (10%) above the prior year's assessment without a vote of the members; any greater increase requires the affirmative vote of Owners of two-thirds (2/3) of the Lots at a meeting called for that purpose.

4.4 Special Assessments. A special assessment for a capital improvement requires the affirmative vote of Owners of two-thirds (2/3) of the Lots at a meeting called for that purpose, at which a quorum of Owners of thirty percent (30%) of the Lots is present in person or by proxy.

4.5 Effect of Nonpayment; Remedies. An assessment not paid within thirty (30) days after it is due bears interest at the lesser of ten percent (10%) per annum and the maximum rate permitted by law. Before the Association may foreclose the assessment lien, it shall send the Owner written notice of the delinquency by certified mail, state the total amount due and the Owner's right to cure, and allow the Owner at least forty-five (45) days to cure or to request a payment plan under Section 209.0062 of the Texas Property Code. The Association may not foreclose a lien consisting solely of fines or of attorneys' fees relating to fines, as provided in Section 209.009 of the Texas Property Code.

4.6 Subordination. The assessment lien is subordinate to the lien of any first mortgage recorded before the assessment became due.

ARTICLE V. USE RESTRICTIONS

5.1 Residential Use. Each Lot shall be used only for single-family residential purposes. No trade or business may be conducted on a Lot, except that an Owner may maintain a home office that generates no customer traffic, signage, or employee presence.

5.2 Leasing. An Owner may lease a Lot for a term of not less than six (6) months. The Owner shall provide the Association with the tenant's name and contact information within ten (10) days after the lease begins, and remains responsible for the tenant's compliance with this Declaration.

5.3 Nuisances. No noxious or offensive activity may be carried on upon any Lot, nor may anything be done on a Lot that is or becomes an annoyance or nuisance to the neighborhood.

5.4 Vehicles. No inoperable vehicle, commercial vehicle over one ton, recreational vehicle, boat, or trailer may be parked on a Lot other than in an enclosed garage, or on a private street, for more than forty-eight (48) hours.

5.5 Solar Devices and Rain Barrels. Nothing in this Declaration prohibits an Owner from installing a solar energy device or a rain barrel except as permitted by Sections 202.010 and 202.007 of the Texas Property Code, and the Board shall review any such application in accordance with those sections.

5.6 Flags and Religious Displays. Nothing in this Declaration prohibits the display of the flag of the United States, the State of Texas, or a religious item on the entry to a dwelling, except as permitted by Sections 202.011 and 202.018 of the Texas Property Code.

ARTICLE VI. ARCHITECTURAL CONTROL

6.1 Approval Required. No building, fence, wall, pool, or other structure may be erected on a Lot, and no exterior alteration may be made, until the plans have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Board or by an architectural review committee the Board appoints.

6.2 Standards and Timing. The Board shall adopt and publish written architectural guidelines. The Board shall approve or deny an application in writing within forty-five (45) days after it receives a complete application, and shall state the reason for any denial. If the Board fails to act within that period, the application is deemed approved.

6.3 Appeal. An Owner whose application is denied may appeal to the full membership at the next regular meeting of the Association.

ARTICLE VII. ENFORCEMENT

7.1 Remedies. The Association or any Owner may enforce this Declaration by any proceeding at law or in equity. Before the Association may levy a fine or suspend a right, it shall give the Owner written notice describing the violation, stating the amount of any proposed fine, and offering the Owner a reasonable period to cure and a right to be heard before the Board, as required by Section 209.006 of the Texas Property Code.

7.2 No Waiver. Failure to enforce any covenant is not a waiver of the right to enforce it later.

ARTICLE VIII. GENERAL PROVISIONS

8.1 Term and Renewal. These covenants run with the land and bind all parties for an initial term of thirty (30) years from the date this Declaration is recorded, after which they are automatically extended for successive periods of ten (10) years unless Owners of at least two-thirds (2/3) of the Lots record an instrument terminating them.

8.2 Amendment. This Declaration may be amended by an instrument signed by Owners of at least two-thirds (2/3) of the Lots and recorded in the Official Public Records of Collin County, Texas. During the Development Period, the Declarant may amend this Declaration unilaterally to correct a scrivener's error, to comply with the requirements of a governmental authority or an institutional lender, or to annex additional property.

8.3 Severability. Invalidation of any covenant by judgment or court order does not affect any other provision, which remains in full force and effect.

8.4 Governing Law. This Declaration is governed by the laws of the State of Texas, including Chapters 202, 204, and 209 of the Texas Property Code.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Declarant has executed this Declaration on the date first written above.
